hard_questions.text: Does a record carry only the CLI-stamped filed_at, or also an agent-supplied occurred-at (an --at flag) for the moment the thing actually happened? If both, occurred-at is the agent's own claim and must render as such
hard_questions.resolution: If per-record timestamps are ever built they are CLI-stamped filed_at only, never an agent-supplied occurred-at; not part of this frame (see the decision claim c17)

claims.text: A read-only 'devague ledger [--json]' verb lists every record across the current frame, its plan and its delivery store in one filing timeline (id, family, status, filed_at, one-line text), so the agent and the human can see the whole ledger without six different --list flags

hard_questions.text: Does 'ledger managed by the CLI' mean only a unified read verb across frame, plan and delivery stores, or also the CLI owning the ledger files' lifecycle (a devague ledger export or commit-ready artifact under docs/ledgers/)?

claims.text: devague status and show surface a third staleness direction beside stale deviations and orphaned evidence: a confirmed claim contradicted by a later approved delta or by a rejected obligation, rendered as a coherence warning that never gates convergence

hard_questions.text: Which pairs count as a contradiction: a confirmed claim named by an approved delta of kind removed or amended; a confirmed claim whose obligation is rejected; both?

claims.text: devague learn's operating rules state one freshness rule for every ledger family, not only obligations: file at the moment it happens, because written late is written flattering (issue 97); the next: hint after a filing move echoes it only when a filing is proposed and unadjudicated

The CLI never estimates, backfills or adjudicates freshness on its own: timestamps are stamped at filing by the CLI, an agent-supplied occurred-at is recorded as a claim of the agent, and no freshness signal ever blocks convergence on either engine (the lapse ledger precedent, tests test_convergence.py and test_plan_convergence.py)

No retroactive timestamp backfill on existing .devague stores: records filed before the schema bump load with filed_at absent and render as 'undated', following the ClaimRevision precedent of a plain field with a default rather than a migration
